- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: model often fails to adjust early in a trend; true price moves faster than forecasted, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature retracement in forecast.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment, underreacting to longer-term structural trends.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs” — if sentiment is rising but price is flat, model may falsely anticipate a peak.
- If sentiment is rising and price is trending up, model should not over-forecast the next peak — allow for gradual consolidation.
- If sentiment is falling and price is rising, model should not assume a reversal — price may continue upward despite sentiment dip.
